transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in today?

I just don’t care about the things I used to love doing anymore, even my projects in the garage and going out on the river. I look at my tools or the water and I just feel completely empty, like there's no point to any of it.
How long have you been feeling this loss of interest and emptiness? Has it been most days for at least two years, or is it a more recent change?

It’s been going on for a little over two years now, starting shortly after the big restructuring at the warehouse. It’s definitely not a recent change—I’ve felt this heavy emptiness almost every single day since then.
During these two years, have you also felt depressed or down most days, or had low energy or poor concentration nearly every day?

Yes, I've felt deeply down and heavy almost every day, and my energy is so low it feels like I'm constantly moving through mud. It's also been incredibly hard to concentrate on basic tasks, whether I'm at the warehouse or just trying to do things around the house. It just feels like a constant, exhausting struggle.
Have you ever had a period of several days or longer when you felt unusually energized or irritable, needed much less sleep, talked more than usual, or did things that were out of character for you?

No, I've never had any periods of high energy or anything like that. It's actually been the exact opposite—I feel constantly slowed down, exhausted, and heavy, like I'm moving through mud. I'm usually very quiet and just feel completely drained all the time.
Have there ever been any periods of at least 2 months during these past two years when you felt back to your normal self, with little or no depression or loss of interest?

No, I haven't had any periods like that where I felt back to my normal self. This heavy, depressed feeling and the complete lack of interest have been there almost every single day for the past two years without any real break.
Have you also had changes in sleep or appetite, low self-esteem, or feelings of hopelessness during this time?

Yes, I lie awake for hours staring at the ceiling and wake up constantly, and my appetite is so gone that my wife has to remind me to eat, which has made me lose a lot of weight. I also feel completely hopeless and guilty, like I've ruined everything at work and am just dragging my family down. It feels like I don't even deserve to be around them anymore.
Have you had any thoughts that you would be better off dead or thoughts of hurting yourself?

I sometimes catch myself thinking they'd be better off without me because I just drag everyone down and don't deserve to be around them. But I don't have any actual plans to hurt myself or do anything like that. It's just this constant, heavy feeling that I'm a burden to my family.
Have you ever heard or seen things that other people could not, or felt that others were trying to harm you or that you were guilty of terrible things that were not true?

Yes, actually... I keep hearing a man's voice right behind me at the warehouse telling me I'm dangerous and going to kill someone, even when there's nobody there. I'm also convinced the company is tracking me through my work badge and the new forklifts just to find an excuse to fire me, and I can't shake the guilt that I've somehow ruined everything for my family and caused the layoffs at work.
Did the hallucinations or paranoid beliefs ever happen for at least 2 weeks when you were not feeling depressed or losing interest, or do they only occur during your depressed periods?

Yes, there was a stretch last year for a few weeks where my mood felt a little better and I wasn't feeling quite so deeply low or crushed. But even during that time, I was still hearing that man's voice telling me I was dangerous and I was still sure they were tracking my work badge.
Have you ever had a period of at least 2 weeks when the hallucinations or paranoid beliefs were still present even though you were not depressed or losing interest at all?

Yes, there was a stretch last year where my mood improved a bit and I wasn't crying as much or feeling quite as crushed. Even during those couple of weeks, I still heard that man's voice telling me I was dangerous and remained convinced my work badge was bugged.
Have you ever had at least 2 weeks when the hallucinations or paranoid beliefs were still present even though you were not depressed or losing interest at all?

Yes, that's right. There was a stretch last year for a few weeks where I wasn't feeling quite as deeply low or crying as much, and my mood seemed a bit better. But even during that time, I still heard that man's voice calling me dangerous and I remained convinced my work badge was bugged.
Have you ever had a period of at least 1 week when you felt unusually high, irritable, or full of energy, needed much less sleep, or became more talkative or impulsive than usual?
No, I have never experienced anything like that. I have never had a period where I felt unusually high, energetic, or talkative.
Have you ever had hallucinations, delusions, or other psychotic symptoms for at least 2 weeks when you were not depressed at all or only had very mild mood symptoms?

Yes, that's exactly what happened last year during that stretch when my mood was much milder and I wasn't feeling as deeply low or crying. Even though the depression had lifted a bit, I still heard that man's voice calling me dangerous and remained convinced my work badge was bugged.
When you are not feeling depressed, do you still hear the voice or believe people are tracking you, or do those symptoms only happen when your depression is severe?

Yes, those things still happen even when I'm not feeling deeply depressed. During that stretch last year when my mood was a bit better and I wasn't feeling as crushed, I still heard that man's voice calling me dangerous and was sure my badge was bugged.
Have you ever had a period of at least 2 weeks when you had hallucinations or strong false beliefs but did not have a major depressive episode at the same time?

Yes, that's exactly what happened during that stretch last year when my mood felt a bit better and I wasn't feeling quite so crushed. Even though the heavy depression wasn't as bad for those few weeks, I still heard that man's voice calling me dangerous and remained convinced my work badge was bugged.
Have you ever had a period of at least 2 weeks when you were hearing the voice or feeling paranoid, but you did not have a major depressive episode at the same time?

Yes, that's right. There was a period last year for a few weeks when my mood lifted and I wasn't crying or feeling so deeply depressed. But even with my mood being better, I still heard that man's voice and was convinced my badge was bugged.
Have you ever had a period of at least 2 weeks when you had hallucinations or strong false beliefs but did not have a major depressive episode at the same time?

Yes, there was a stretch last year when my mood lifted slightly and I wasn't feeling quite as deeply low or crying as much. But even during those few weeks, I still heard that man's voice calling me dangerous and remained convinced my work badge was bugged.

opening_question.question: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient meets criteria for a schizoaffective disorder, depressive type: there is a prolonged major depressive syndrome lasting over 2 years with anhedonia, depressed mood, low energy, poor concentration, insomnia, appetite/weight loss, guilt, hopelessness, and passive death wishes. Psychotic symptoms are also present (auditory hallucinations and persecutory delusions), and critically they persisted for at least 2 weeks during a period when depressive symptoms were only mild/improved, establishing psychosis outside a major depressive episode. This rules out psychotic depression alone.
